title: alint agent report (v1)
description: Output schema emitted by `alint check --format agent`. Optimised for AI coding agents that consume alint inside their own self-correction loops. Differs from `--format json` by (1) flattening rule-results into a single `violations` array, (2) adding a templated `agent_instruction` per violation, (3) reporting `severity` as a lowercase string rather than the SARIF mapping, and (4) flattening non-remediation `analysis_failures` separately. The format is stable behind `schema_version: 1`; field additions are non-breaking, removals or semantic changes bump the version.

schema_version.description: Report schema version. Always 1 for this schema.

format.description: Format discriminator. Always the literal string "agent" for this schema; lets a multi-format consumer route on a single field.

fixable_violations.description: Subset of total_violations that a bare `alint fix` resolves (a Safe, applicable fix), counted per-violation; an Unsafe or `can_fix`-declined finding is not counted. An agent uses this to decide whether to suggest `alint fix`.

total_analysis_failures.description: Count of operational failures that prevented a rule from obtaining a verdict.

notes.description: Present when the report contains non-violation notes. Notes never enter the violations array or affect summary failure counts.

count.description: Total non-violation notes in this report.

details_format.description: Rerun the same check with this output format to retrieve the full per-rule note list.

severity.description: Lowercase severity string. `off` rules don't produce violations and never appear here.

rule_id.description: Rule id, matches the `id:` field of a rule in the config.

file.description: Repo-relative path; absent for tree-wide violations.

human_message.description: The rule's violation message sanitized of terminal controls, bidi overrides/isolates, zero-width characters, and astral tag characters, suitable for human review and LLM consumption.

agent_instruction.description: Templated remediation phrasing optimised for an LLM to act on. Composed from severity, sanitized message, sanitized location, fix availability, and sanitized policy URL (stripped of terminal controls, bidi overrides/isolates, zero-width characters, and astral tag characters).

fix_available.description: Whether a bare `alint fix` resolves THIS violation (a Safe, applicable fix). Per-violation, mirroring `check --format json`'s `fixable`: an Unsafe fix, or one whose `can_fix` declines this finding, is false here even if the rule declares a fixer.

fix_command.description: The `alint` argv that fixes this violation (e.g. ["fix", "--only", "<rule>"]). Present only for a fix-available finding.

proposed_edit.description: The concrete Safe edit(s) `alint fix` would apply to resolve this violation. Present only for a fix-available finding when every target path has an exact JSON string representation; use `fix_command` otherwise.

policy_url.description: Optional documentation URL provided by the rule, sanitized of terminal controls and invisible formatting characters (or "<redacted>" when the URL carried a redacted environment value).

file.description: Repo-relative resource path; absent for repository-wide failures.

human_message.description: The analysis failure message sanitized of terminal controls, bidi overrides/isolates, zero-width characters, and astral tag characters, suitable for human review and LLM consumption.

proposed_edit.description: A concrete fix edit: replace `region` of `path` with `inserted` (empty for a pure deletion).

path.description: Repo-relative path of the edited file.
